title: Go to your first Friday prayer
whyMatters: Jumuah is the Friday congregational prayer, once a week. It can become one of the better hours of your week, though the first time it may just feel like a lot of people in one room. Knowing the shape of it beforehand takes most of the nerves out.

exactActions.text: Check the time before you go
subSteps: Friday prayer times are often different from the usual Dhuhr time.
Many masjids run more than one service.
Check parking, which entrance to use, and the women's space if that applies to you.
If you can, have a full-body wash (ghusl) before you go and wear clean clothes. The wash is recommended, not a condition of the prayer, and wudu alone is valid.
Give yourself time to find the entrance and the shoe area.
Sit quietly and listen to the khutbah.
If you do arrive late, join the row calmly and follow the imam. The salah companion explains how to join late and what to make up.
The imam gives a sermon, then leads two units of prayer.
You can follow the movements of the people around you.
Say Ameen with everyone when the imam finishes Al-Fatihah, and move after the imam, not before him.
If you felt lost, ask someone about it afterwards.

exactActions.text: Talk to one person before you leave
subSteps: Ask about classes for new Muslims or about finding a mentor.
If it is too busy for that, send an email later in the day.
You do not have to stay for a long social visit.

timeEstimate: 45 to 90 minutes, depending on the masjid

obstacles.solution: Try a smaller masjid, get there earlier, or go to a quieter daily prayer first. Your first Jumuah does not have to be your first time inside a masjid.

obstacles.problem: I do not understand the sermon
obstacles.solution: Some khutbahs are partly or entirely in another language. Look for a masjid that gives the khutbah in English, or ask someone for the short version afterwards.

tinyVersion: Look up one masjid's Friday prayer time and plan to get there 15 minutes early.
unlocksNext: Jumuah gives you a weekly rhythm and the easiest place to hear about classes, mentors, and people worth knowing.

contextNotes.title: Work or school
contextNotes.body: If Friday prayer clashes with your schedule, ask a local imam how to handle it and how to word a request for the time.

contextNotes.title: During the sermon
contextNotes.body: Listen quietly and keep your phone away. Do not step over people to reach the front. Sit where there is space, even at the back. If you arrive during the sermon, ask your teacher whether to pray two short rak'ahs first, because scholars differ on it.
